record.title: EnSIMem links structured memory indexes to source-grounded conversational evidence
record.summary: EnSIMem stores dialogue-grounded entity/property indexes as addresses into theme-coherent episodes, then decomposes a query into evidence requirements and retrieves the original source turns needed to answer it. The authors report LoCoMo overall accuracy of 90.6% under GPT-4o-mini and 90.0% under Qwen3-32B, and LongMemEval accuracy of 92.8% under both evaluators. A fixed LoCoMo ablation reports 96.59% for structured entity/type/property retrieval versus 86.36% for dense retrieval. These are paper-reported, LLM-evaluated results. The reported online latency is 14.4 seconds versus 5.70 seconds for MEMORA(P); some comparator rows are transcribed rather than rerun.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On LoCoMo, the authors report EnSIMem overall accuracy of 90.6% when evaluated by GPT-4o-mini and 90.0% with Qwen3-32B; these evaluator-specific scores are reported separately.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On LongMemEval, the authors report 92.8% overall with both GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3-32B evaluators. The comparison rows for other methods are transcribed from prior work rather than rerun in this study.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A fixed LoCoMo retrieval ablation reports 96.59% accuracy for structured entity/type/property retrieval versus 86.36% for dense retrieval, with answer and evaluator models held fixed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports 14.4 seconds mean online latency for EnSIMem versus 5.70 seconds for MEMORA(P); the authors note different token-accounting conventions and that MEMORA does not report separate generation latency.

evidence_gaps.description: EnSIMem's benchmark results and retrieval ablations have not been independently reproduced in this activation; benchmark-wide baseline parity is not fully established.
The reported online latency is substantially higher than the cited MEMORA(P) result, and comparisons of context tokens may use different accounting conventions.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported benchmark results generalize, indexing entities and properties while preserving links to original dialogue could improve evidence-grounded recall in long-running conversational agents. This is notable for episodic-memory design, but the evidence is author-reported, LLM-judged and does not cover procedural skills or semantic consolidation; the reported online latency is also higher than the cited comparator.
limitations: The benchmarks evaluate episodic conversational recall, not procedural skill execution or long-term semantic consolidation.
Scores rely on LLM-based segmentation, extraction, planning and answer evaluation; model changes may affect intermediate representations.
EnSIMem's reported online latency is 14.4s versus 5.70s for MEMORA(P), with the additional cost in planning and retrieval.
Several benchmark-wide comparison rows are transcribed from prior work; the paper reports a local protocol-check rerun for MEMORA(P), not a full matched rerun of all baselines.
No independent reproduction or artifact audit was performed in this activation.

The authors report LoCoMo overall accuracy of 90.6% under GPT-4o-mini and 90.0% under Qwen3-32B, and LongMemEval accuracy of 92.8% under both evaluators. A fixed LoCoMo ablation reports 96.59% for structured entity/type/property retrieval versus 86.36% for dense retrieval. These are paper-reported, LLM-evaluated results. technical.claimed_result: Author-reported evaluator-specific overall scores are 90.6%/90.0% on LoCoMo and 92.8%/92.8% on LongMemEval. A fixed LoCoMo retrieval ablation reports 96.59% structured versus 86.36% dense-only accuracy.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports 14.4 seconds mean online latency for EnSIMem versus 5.70 seconds for MEMORA(P), with additional time concentrated in requirement-aware planning and retrieval. Offline construction is excluded. Token accounting across systems may differ.
technical.demonstrated_result: No independent reproduction was conducted in this review. The benchmark scores remain CLAIMED author-reported results.
technical.implementation_status: The paper links code packages for both benchmark suites and reports prompts/configurations. This activation did not execute the implementation.
technical.mechanism: Offline construction partitions dialogue into theme-coherent episodes and indexes entity/type/property values linked to original turns. Online planning decomposes a request into evidence requirements and query type, then combines structured matching with dense fallback and adaptively retrieves until requirement coverage is met; answers use restored source turns.
technical.regime: The paper evaluates episodic conversational recall on LoCoMo and LongMemEval using GPT-4.1-mini for answer generation and GPT-4o-mini plus Qwen3-32B as separate LLM evaluators. Reported online latency excludes offline memory construction.
technical.reproducibility: The full v2 paper, benchmark tables and limitations were inspected. Results use LLM answer evaluation at temperature 0; two evaluators are reported separately. Independent reproduction and baseline parity audit remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the LoCoMo retrieval ablation, dense retrieval only under the same answer and GPT-4o-mini evaluator setup. Published benchmark-wide comparator rows are partly transcribed; the authors locally reran MEMORA(P) as a protocol check at 86.23% versus its published 86.3% LoCoMo score.

brief.title: EnSIMem links structured memory indexes to source-grounded conversational evidence
brief.why_it_matters: The design treats an index as an address to preserved dialogue, rather than as a lossy replacement for source evidence. It pairs entity/property matching with query-specific coverage planning and restores original turns before answer generation. If reproduced, this could inform memory systems that need temporal, compositional or multi-fact recall; practical use trades more explicit evidence handling for higher reported online latency.
